rich_summary: Sanjaya recounts how the frightened king Jayadratha, after hearing of Arjuna’s vow to kill him for Abhimanyu’s death, seeks reassurance from Drona. Drona admits that although Jayadratha and Arjuna received equal training, Arjuna surpasses him through discipline and yogic practice, yet he promises protection and reminds him that a warrior’s death leads to heavenly reward. Encouraged, Jayadratha resolves to fight. Later Krishna rebukes Arjuna for rashly vowing Jayadratha’s death without consultation, warning of the danger. Meanwhile the Kauravas, terrified by the vow, plan elaborate defenses: Drona will arrange a complex battle formation, and six great warriors will guard Jayadratha so that Arjuna must defeat them first. The passage builds tension for the coming battle and underscores Arjuna’s formidable reputation.

highlight_spans.why: Opening narration where Sanjaya frames Jayadratha seeking counsel from Drona, setting the strategic and emotional stakes.
The early exchange leading into Drona’s assessment, a pivotal comparison between Jayadratha and Arjuna.
Captures the anxious tone surrounding Jayadratha’s fear and search for reassurance before facing Arjuna.

top_scenes.scene_text: Jayadratha humbly bowing before the aged warrior Drona in a dimly lit war tent at night, seeking reassurance about facing Arjuna.
Krishna sternly addressing Arjuna beside the chariot, warning him about the rash vow while the Pandava camp glows with torches.
A vast battlefield diagram coming to life: Drona’s complex lotus-and-cart formation with Jayadratha hidden at its center guarded by six mighty warriors.
